_comment: Allowlist for scripts/check_test_weakening.py (Layer 4, #52). Replaced the ALLOW_TEST_WEAKEN=1 environment override on 2026-08-08 — that was a blanket, invisible, whole-run bypass that silenced every file at once, left no trace in the reviewed diff, and was wired to a PR label in both CI workflows so it could be set from outside the repo. Each entry sanctions ONE file's deletion with an EXACT delta and a written reason. Governance mirrors .health-endpoint-allowlist.json / .urllib-httperror-close-allowlist.json: rationale >= 40 chars, malformed entries hard-fail. Two rules are specific to this guard: (1) an entry grants exactly its recorded allowed_delta — a measured delta WORSE than the entry fails, so an entry can never absorb future weakening of the same file; (2) a file with no entry fails as before. DO NOT widen an allowed_delta to make a new failure go away: that converts a one-time sanction into a permanent licence for the file, which is the hole this mechanism replaced.
_stale_policy: A STALE entry (file absent from the branch diff, or measured delta better than recorded) is a WARNING printed on every run, NOT a hard error — deliberately unlike the sibling allowlists, whose input is the filesystem. This guard diffs against merge-base(origin/master, HEAD), which MOVES: the moment a branch carrying an entry merges, its file leaves the diff and the entry goes stale through nobody's fault, and hard-failing would turn master red for everyone. The two ADR-0215 train entries this file used to carry (test_scope_filter_e2e.py, test_v5_42_2_branch_default_e2e.py) were removed on 2026-08-12 by 0047 C15a under exactly that instruction: the train had merged, both files were absent from BOTH merge-base 92dbb4b5 and HEAD, so neither could ever re-enter the branch diff and neither entry could ever stop warning. An entry whose staleness is unresolvable is noise that teaches the next reader to skim the warnings — delete it as this policy directs, and never widen an allowed_delta to silence one.
_entries: Three entries. Task 379 widened the scan from the e2e subset to every yadgar/tests/**/*.py, which made the guard capable of seeing the relaxation it was filed for. Recording them here is the point of the mechanism: the sanction is written down where review happens, instead of the scan being re-narrowed until the failure disappears.

yadgar/tests/scripts/test_migration_014_.rationale: Gate-honesty car I: FALSE RED removed, not coverage. These five tests assert a NON-ZERO backfill count, which requires a real embedding vector; sentence-transformers lives in the optional [ml] extra, so under plain `make test` (`--extra test`) EmbeddingEngine returned None for every row and they measured `assert 0 == 4` / `0 == 1` / `0 == 6`. Measured 2026-08-27: 5 failed / 13 passed on a venv synced `--extra dev --extra test`; 19 passed (this file + the sibling recall test) on one synced `--extra dev --extra test --extra ml --extra sql --extra analytics`. Standing failures that are not bugs train readers to skim red — the mirror of the false green this train exists to kill. The guards are pytest.importorskip('sentence_transformers') and are sanctioned CONDITIONALLY in yadgar/tests/skip_inventory.json (ml-extra-embedding-backfill-01, `sanctioned_when_module_absent`), so the skip gate FAILS a leg that installed the extra and skipped them anyway — this cannot hide a regression. Verified both directions: the same skip lines under a MEASURED `sentence_transformers=present` receipt exit 1. Deliberately scoped to the five that actually failed, not the whole class: test_returns_zero_on_empty_db and test_backfill_embed_failure_warns_and_skips pass on their own merits without the extra and still run under `make test`. ADR-0087 governs the inventory side.

yadgar/tests/scripts/test_v5_42_5_direct.rationale: Gate-honesty car I, same mechanism, one test. test_every_candidate_query_carries_the_scope_predicate ends with four liveness assertions that stop `no unscoped queries` being vacuously true; one requires the memory VECTOR arm to have issued its query, which needs a real query embedding from the [ml] extra. Measured absent it failed with `memory vector arm did not run` on every plain `make test` run — false RED with no bug behind it. TRADE-OFF recorded rather than hidden: the guard skips the WHOLE test, so the SQL-level scope-predicate assertion also stops running under plain `make test`. Making only the vector-arm assertion conditional would be a weakened assertion, which is worse, and CI plus `make test-ci` install `--extra ml` so the check still runs where it gates merges. Sanctioned CONDITIONALLY in yadgar/tests/skip_inventory.json (ml-extra-recall-vector-arm-01): the skip gate FAILS if this ever skips on a leg where sentence_transformers is measured PRESENT.

yadgar/tests/backend/test_project_regist.rationale: FILE DELETED, not weakened. car/T-dead-code-purge removed yadgar/backend/admin_exec/project_registry.py entirely: _ensure_project_exists_async and _ensure_project_exists_sync had ZERO production call sites (Car 5 proved it, and identity_stamp.py documented it), and what remained was a _live_engine used only by that pair plus a re-export of two error classes _shared/storage/sql/errors.py already owns. The live registry guard is MariaStorageEngine.assert_project_registered (_shared/storage/sql/registry.py), which is covered by test_c6_project_registry_writer.py and the new refresh=False preview tests. Deleting a test whose subject no longer exists is not a coverage loss; this entry records that judgement rather than hiding it. Ledger task 384.
